1.why: Sans-serif typeface with clear headings, adequate line spacing and generous white space in the cards, though the Logs panel and code lists use small monospace text that is tighter.

2.why: No italics or all-caps are used and instructional text is limited to one or two short sentences per screen; only the dark Logs block is a dense monospace mass of text.

3.why: Layout is a single narrow centred column that would reflow reasonably on a phone, but the two-column recovery-code grid, wide monospace secret string and log lines would be cramped and no actual mobile viewport is evidenced.

4.why: Each step uses short plain-language instructions such as 'Enter the six-digit identity code' and 'Each recovery code works once', with minimal jargon beyond 'authenticator'/'provisioning'.

5.why: Placeholders demonstrate expected formats — 'marcus@example.com', '15551234567', '6 digits', 'ABCD-1234-EF56-7890' — although the identity verification code field on step 2 has no placeholder example.

6.why: No screen requires reading more than a two- or three-line paragraph before acting; the longest text is the three-line regeneration warning.

7.why: No copy buttons, download or print options appear anywhere — the authenticator secret and the eight recovery codes are shown as plain static text that must be transcribed by hand.

8.why: Step 4 offers only a text 'Provisioning information' string and explicitly says manual entry is an alternative to scanning, but no QR code or scannable equivalent is actually rendered.

9.why: Fields have visible labels but there is no evidence of autocomplete attributes, and one-off simulated code fields plus a plain-text 'Manual secret entry' box give no indication of password-manager or autofill integration.

10.why: Each screen has a single bold heading and a prominent solid blue primary button, though there is no step indicator (e.g. 'Step 2 of 5') to show position in the flow.

11.why: Most screens ask one thing, but step 4 presents 'Create authenticator setup', 'Manual secret entry', 'Authenticator code' and 'Confirm authenticator' together, and the MFA settings screen exposes four competing buttons at once.

12.why: Confirmations such as 'Authenticator verification succeeded.', 'Recovery code accepted and permanently consumed.' and 'Challenge ready. Enter the test code from Logs.' state what happened, but they rarely state what comes next and screens change with no forward guidance.

13.why: Retry is possible ('Start over', re-submitting codes, 'Regenerate recovery codes'), but codes cannot be revealed/hidden or re-requested — recovery codes are shown once and never again, and there is no way to re-display the authenticator secret after leaving the page.

14.why: The only error observed, 'The request could not be completed.', names neither the problem nor any remedy, giving the user no actionable information.

15.why: No countdown timer or session-expiry warning is visible on any screen, but neither is any explicit reassurance about time, and the TOTP/challenge nature implies unseen expiry windows.
